replication.target_description: Empirical audiovisual sensory noise versus each participant’s best (minimum-noise) unisensory condition; within-participant bootstrap comparisons, section 3.4.1/Fig. 3B. No group-level d/p for this exact contrast is printed in the supplied main report.

es.location: Section 3.4.1, Fig. 3B caption and accompanying text; methods section 2.13.1
es.quote: B. Empirical audiovisual sensory noise parameters versus the minimum of the auditory or visual sensory noise parameters. The colour of the diamonds' outlines indicates the least variable unisensory modality for each participant ( A = green, V = red). Dark diamonds indicate twenty-four participants with a significant multisensory variance reduction.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical PMC full-report parse: title Integration of audiovisual spatial signals is not consistent with maximum likelihood estimation; authors David Meijer, Sebastijan Veselič, Carmelo Calafiore, Uta Noppeney; Cortex 119:74–88 (2019); DOI 10.1016/j.cortex.2019.03.026. Methods, Results, Discussion and references are present; supplementary DOCX is linked but not supplied. No PDF was supplied, so page-10 layout could not be inspected. Original and unassigned fields are placeholders only. The description identifies Fig. 3B and its within-participant comparisons. Twenty-four significant individual results are reported, without individual numerical p values or a group-level effect size. No d was computed. The section 3.3 empirical-versus-MLE-predicted test (t(35)=.33, p=.37, dz=.06) is a different contrast and is not assigned to this row. The generic bootstrap significance rule is not treated as a numerical same-test p bound.
